observations: Mutable default argument `bucket=[]` is created once at function definition time and shared across all calls that omit the argument.
The behavior contract states each omitted-bucket call should get a fresh bucket, but the code reuses the same list object, so the contract is violated.
Probe p1: first call collect(1) returns [1]; second call collect(2) returns [1, 2] because the same default list is mutated, not a fresh [2].
Probe p2: collect(3, [9]) appends to the explicit list and returns [9, 3], which matches the contract for explicit buckets.
The default list is also mutated by any omitted-bucket call, so state leaks across calls and persists for the module lifetime.
No static findings were supplied, but the mutable-default pattern is the observable defect.
